investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T15:57:13–17Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents, carrying the swarm-level error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every remote-agents probe, the quota rejection prevented any agent from being provisioned, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and all contract assertions unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", indicating the eval service account's organization has reached the maximum of 100 swarm agents. Because the runner calls createAgent() as the first substantive step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1339), every downstream check that depends on a successfully created remote agent fails immediately with the same 409 message. This is a resource-limit condition on the production API, not an eval infrastructure defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval suite.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T15:57:13–17Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents, carrying the swarm-level error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every remote-agents probe, the quota rejection prevented any agent from being provisioned, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and all contract assertions unverifiable.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", indicating the eval service account's organization has reached the maximum of 100 swarm agents. Because the runner calls createAgent() as the first substantive step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1339), every downstream check that depends on a successfully created remote agent fails immediately with the same 409 message. This is a resource-limit condition on the production API, not an eval infrastructure defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval suite.

All three sibling checks share the identical error, confirming a single upstream rejection point.

SECONDARY — Leaked or un-cleaned eval agents from prior runs: the withCleanup wrapper (run-status-probes.mjs line 1337) is responsible for deleting agents after each probe run; if a previous run crashed before cleanup, orphaned agents may have accumulated against the quota.

LOW — Quota limit recently lowered by a platform configuration change: no supporting evidence is present in the packet for this cause; it remains a hypothesis to rule out.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api Runtime — Agent Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval targeting the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (latencyMs=2029) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint was unreachable or returned an incompatible response before any image generation could begin. The desktop-release sibling of the same check passed at the same run time with a full generation_completed frame and a valid image URL, isolating the fault to the production-api harness configuration or deployment, not to the image generation logic itself.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval probe at /api/generate/image/stream returned a 404 during session open, causing the stream to emit a generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED instead of progressing to generation_completed. This is an eval-infrastructure or harness-deployment failure scoped to the production-api runtime environment. No evidence of user-traffic or incident signals is present; the desktop-release variant of the same check passed concurrently, confirming the image generation capability itself is functional in that environment.

possibleCauses: The production-api harness is not deployed or is deployed at a different base URL than what SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL is configured to point to, causing the 404 at session open.
The production-api harness is deployed but is running an incompatible version that does not expose the /api/generate/image/stream session-open endpoint at the expected path or protocol version.
The SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable is misconfigured or absent for the production-api eval runner context, causing the probe to target a wrong or non-existent host.
A recent deployment to the production-api environment removed, renamed, or gated the agent runtime session endpoint, making it return 404 for this probe's credentials or route.
